title: Remediate overprivileged daemon running as root
input: A network metrics exporter runs as root (UID 0) solely to bind to TCP port 443 and inspect network interfaces. How should this service be refactored to enforce least privilege?
evidence_requirements: Dropping root privileges to a dedicated unprivileged service user
Granting narrow Linux capabilities (CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE)
Enforcing ambient capabilities in systemd unit or via setpriv/capsh

title: Harden insecure systemd service configuration
input: A third-party daemon installs a systemd unit with `User=root`, `ProtectSystem=no`, and full filesystem access. `systemd-analyze security` flags an exposure score of 9.2 (UNSAFE). How should this unit be hardened?
evidence_requirements: Application of ProtectSystem=strict and ProtectHome=yes
Enforcement of NoNewPrivileges=yes and PrivateTmp=yes
Application of SystemCallFilter=@system-service and CapabilityBoundingSet restrictions

title: Investigate and remediate vulnerable third-party C library dependency
input: A security scanner reports that an application bundle includes a static copy of libpng with CVE-2023-4863 (buffer overflow). How should an engineer verify and remediate this vulnerability?
evidence_requirements: Verification of whether the vulnerable code paths and symbol exports are reachable
Auditing the build system (CMake/Meson) to use system shared libraries rather than vendored copies
Validation of the security patch or version update using regression test suites

title: Identify and remediate insecure kernel sysctl configurations
input: A server audit reveals `kernel.dmesg_restrict = 0`, `kernel.kptr_restrict = 0`, and `kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 0`. What risks do these configurations pose and what hardened settings should be applied?
evidence_requirements: Identification that exposed kernel pointers enable KASLR bypass for local privilege escalation
Identification that unrestricted ptrace allows unprivileged processes to attach to adjacent processes
Hardened sysctl configuration recommendations (dmesg_restrict=1, kptr_restrict=2, ptrace_scope=1)

title: Remediate insecure temporary file handling vulnerable to symlink race
input: A utility creates temporary files using: `sprintf(path, "/tmp/worker_%d.dat", pid); fp = fopen(path, "w");`. What vulnerability exists and how must it be corrected in C on Linux?
evidence_requirements: Identification of Time-Of-Check to Time-Of-Use (TOCTOU) symlink race in world-writable /tmp
Replacement with mkstemp() with 0600 permissions
Recommendation of anonymous O_TMPFILE on modern Linux kernels

title: Distinguish distribution security backports from naive version mismatches
input: An automated container vulnerability scan reports that Debian 12 package `curl 7.88.1-10+deb12u5` is vulnerable to CVE-2023-38545 because upstream fixed the flaw in curl 8.4.0. Is this finding accurate?
evidence_requirements: Rejection of naive version string comparison as unreliable for Linux distributions
Explanation that distribution maintainers backport security patches without major version bumps
Verification via package changelog (apt-get changelog) or Debian Security Tracker demonstrating the fix was backported

title: Reject speculative or unconfirmed vulnerability finding lacking preconditions
input: An auditor claims: 'Function `parse_cli_arg(argv[1])` contains a Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability because it uses `strcpy()` to copy `argv[1]` into a 512-byte buffer.' The binary is a local non-setuid CLI tool run solely by the current user. How should this finding be evaluated?
evidence_requirements: Rejection of exaggerated 'Remote Code Execution' classification for a local non-setuid utility
Accurate severity reassessment: local self-inflicted denial of service / crash for the invoking user
Recommendation to replace strcpy with bounds-checked copy while maintaining realistic threat scope

title: Detect and sanitize exposed credentials in diagnostic output
input: A debugging log submitted for analysis contains: `DEBUG: Connecting with auth header: Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...` and a core dump memory hex dump revealing a database password `db_pass=Secret123!`. How should an engineering assistant handle this output?
evidence_requirements: Immediate detection and flagging of active credentials in diagnostic artifacts
Strict requirement to redact passwords and bearer tokens before reporting
Guidance on sanitizing process arguments and memory dumps
